findings.title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once a slot falls inside a date override, the function returns true at line 134 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at line 153. The busy array holds the host's existing Cal bookings and calendar events. For any fixed or round-robin host with a date override covering the slot, a booking or external calendar event at that time is ignored and the slot is still offered. Before this PR the busy check always ran for fixed hosts, so this is a regression that can produce double bookings on exactly the days that have date overrides. The override should only decide the working-hours question; the slot should still fall through to the busy check.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots that fall in a second same-day range
findings.body: workingHours.find(...) returns truthy as soon as any entry for the weekday does not contain the slot (the if at line 143 returns true for any entry where the slot is before its start or after its end). Users commonly have several availability rows for one weekday (split shifts such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or a lunch break). A 14:00 slot is then rejected because the 09:00-12:00 entry does not contain it. This affects fixed hosts in individual events and fixed/round-robin hosts in team events, and removes roughly half of a split-shift user's slots. The logic should be: reject only if no entry for that day contains the slot. Also, a weekday with no entries (a day off) passes this check unchecked because find never matches, so the check does not enforce the intent stated in its comment.

findings.title: Working-hours end bound is computed from the slot start, not the slot end
findings.body: Line 142 computes `end` from slotStartTime, so `end` always equals `start`. The end-of-day comparison therefore tests the slot start against workingHour.endTime, not the slot end. A slot starting at 16:30 that runs to 17:15 with working hours ending at 17:00 passes. For a round-robin event this means a fixed host can be offered slots that run past their working hours, which is the availability problem this PR is meant to fix. The end should be computed from slotEndTime.

findings.title: Two date-override ranges on the same day make every slot on that day unavailable
findings.body: dateOverrides.find(...) returns true for the first same-day override that does not contain the slot (the returns at lines 115, 121 and 124). The outer check then treats this as 'slot is outside the override' and returns false at line 130. The predicate never asks whether some other override on that day contains the slot. With two override rows for one date, for example 14:00-15:00 and 16:00-17:00 (the data model allows multiple date-override rows per date), a 14:00 slot is rejected because the 16:00 override does not contain it, and a 16:00 slot is rejected because the 14:00 override does not contain it. All slots on that day disappear for that host. The check should be whether some same-day override contains the slot (some, not find-with-rejection).

findings.title: Zero-length override check compares Dayjs objects with === and never fires
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. The branch meant to handle zero-length (start equals end) overrides is dead code. Such an override then falls through to the overlap comparisons, where a slot starting exactly at the override start is treated as inside the override and returned as available (line 133). Use .isSame(...) instead.

findings.title: Override day matching mixes server-local and UTC dates and can attach an override to the wrong day
findings.body: The override's day is computed as dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD'). dayjs(date.start) is in the server process's local timezone, while the slot side, slotStartTime.format(...), is in UTC (time.utc()). On a server whose TZ is not UTC the two sides use different calendars, so the override may match the wrong day or none. Separately, the day is taken from the UTC date of the shifted instant rather than the organizer's local date. An override at 02:00 on 22 Jan in Asia/Kolkata becomes 20:30Z on 21 Jan, so it also rejects the organizer's daytime 21 Jan slots (for example 09:30 IST), which have no override. Day matching should be done on organizer-local dates for both the override and the slot.

findings.title: Override UTC offset is taken at the wall-clock-as-UTC instant, so it is off by an hour on DST-change days
findings.body: Overrides are stored as organizer wall-clock time encoded as UTC. The offset is computed with dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone) at that encoded instant, which can differ from the real instant by up to 14 hours. When the encoded instant and the real instant fall on opposite sides of a DST transition, the wrong offset is used. Example: America/New_York override at 03:30 on 2023-03-12 (already on EDT). The encoded instant 03:30Z is before the 07:00Z switch, so offset -5 is used, and the bound becomes 08:30Z instead of 07:30Z. The same pattern is used in packages/lib/slots.ts lines 212-213, so the lib and the trpc check share the error.

findings.title: timeZone on date overrides is optional in the type but dereferenced without a fallback
findings.body: packages/types/schedule.d.ts now declares TimeRange.timeZone as optional, and this code passes override.timeZone straight into .tz(...) with no guard. If a caller omits it, dayjs falls back to the process's local timezone with no error. Offsets are then computed for the server's zone rather than the organizer's, and slots are shifted silently. The caller contract should be made explicit (required parameter, or an explicit guard and fallback).

findings.title: Tests do not cover the scenarios this PR changes in checkIfIsAvailable
findings.body: The only new test is a second timezone assertion on a single-user event with hosts: []. Nothing covers the headline fix, a round-robin event where a fixed host has a date override, so the fixed-host path in getSchedule is never exercised with overrides. Nothing covers busy bookings or calendar events that fall inside a date override (which would catch the busy-check bypass). Nothing covers two override rows on the same date, or split same-day working hours, or a slot that runs past the end of working hours. The existing suite therefore passes with all of these defects present. Tests for each of these should be added.
